greeting.buildAutomationDescription: Connect various nodes to automate complex tasks. Each node handles specific functions, and data flows sequentially for processing.
greeting.chatbotToolDescription: The main purpose of workflows is to use them as tools in chatbot conversations. Turn repetitive tasks into workflows for easy execution during chats.
greeting.parameterBasedDescription: Input nodes define parameter structures, not triggers. They specify the data format needed when chatbot calls this workflow as a tool.
greeting.exampleDescription: Create an "Email Writing → Translation → Send" workflow, then easily execute it in chatbot conversations with "@email_workflow".
greeting.ctaMessage: Start creating workflows now to expand your chatbot's capabilities!

kindsDescription.input:
Define input parameters that the chatbot will provide when using this workflow as a tool.

Specify the data structure and validation rules for tool execution.
kindsDescription.output:
Collect and return the final results from your workflow execution.

Combine data from multiple nodes into the final tool response.
kindsDescription.llm:
Generate text or structured data using AI models.

Reference previous node outputs with '/' mentions to create context-aware responses.

Use Structured Output to transform, format, and validate data - not just for text generation.
kindsDescription.tool:
Execute MCP tools or external services.

Write instructions in messages, and LLM will generate the required tool parameters from your context.
kindsDescription.note:
Add documentation and comments to organize your workflow logic.

Help team members understand complex workflow processes.
kindsDescription.code:
Execute custom code scripts with access to previous node data.

Run JavaScript, Python, or other languages within your workflow (coming soon).
kindsDescription.http:
Fetch data from external APIs and web services via HTTP requests.

Integrate with REST APIs, webhooks, and third-party services.
kindsDescription.template:
Create dynamic documents by combining text with data from previous nodes.

Generate emails, reports, or formatted content using variable substitution.
kindsDescription.condition:
Add conditional logic to branch your workflow based on data evaluation.

Create if-else logic to handle different scenarios and data conditions.

website.name: Website analytics
website.help: Reads the site_events table that your marketing site's collector writes to its Supabase project.

supabaseUrl.label: Supabase project URL
supabaseUrl.help: The marketing site's project, e.g. https://xyz.supabase.co

supabaseSecretKey.label: Secret key
supabaseSecretKey.help: Server secret key (sb_secret_… or service role). Only site_events is read.

vercel.name: Vercel
vercel.help: Production deployment state for up to six projects.

token.label: Access token
token.help: Vercel → Account settings → Tokens. Read access is enough.

teamId.label: Team ID
teamId.help: Leave blank to detect the team from the token. Otherwise the team ID (team_…) or the slug from the Vercel URL.

projects.label: Projects
projects.help: One per line: LABEL = prj_…, or just the project ID or name (up to six). The label names the engine and is matched against Superlog service names.

stripe.name: Stripe
stripe.help: Balance, MRR, payments, failed payments and the next payout. Use a restricted key, never the secret key.

restrictedKey.label: Restricted key
restrictedKey.help: rk_live_… or rk_test_… with read access to Balance, Subscriptions, Charges and Payouts.

revolut.name: Revolut Business
revolut.help: Balances, cash flow and recent transactions. In Revolut Business → APIs, upload the public certificate, set the redirect URI and enable access, then paste the authorization code here once.

privateKeyPem.label: Private key (PEM)
privateKeyPem.help: The key whose public certificate you uploaded to Revolut.

authorizationCode.label: Authorization code
authorizationCode.help: After enabling access, Revolut redirects with ?code=…. Paste it and save: it is exchanged for a refresh token once and not stored.

refreshToken.label: Refresh token
refreshToken.help: Filled from the authorization code. Freelancer plans expire it after 90 days.

issuer.label: Redirect URI domain
issuer.help: Domain of the redirect URI set in Revolut (JWT issuer). Defaults to this app's domain.

largeTransactionThreshold.label: Alert threshold
largeTransactionThreshold.help: Transactions at or above this amount post an alert to UPDATES. Default 5000.

superlog.name: Superlog
superlog.help: Open incidents, firing alerts and error logs, read through Superlog's MCP server.

token.label: MCP token
token.help: Personal access token (superlog_pat_…) from Superlog → Settings → MCP tokens. The ingest key (sl_public_…) does not work here.

seo.name: SEO (OpenSEO / DataForSEO)
seo.help: Organic traffic, keyword rankings and referring domains through an SEO MCP server.

mcpServerId.label: MCP server
mcpServerId.help: OpenSEO signs in with OAuth only: add https://app.openseo.so/mcp under MCP servers, authorize it, then pick it here.

mcpUrl.label: MCP server URL
mcpUrl.help: DataForSEO without an MCP server only. Leave blank for the default endpoint.
